admin_token.description: The admin token, for resources that use the `/admin` API. This requires the admin page to be enabled. Can also be set with the `VAULTWARDEN_ADMIN_TOKEN` environment variable.

client_id.description: The `client_id` of the user's personal API key, to log in with the API key instead of the master password, for example when two-step login is enabled. Requires `email` and `master_password`. Can also be set with the `VAULTWARDEN_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.

client_secret.description: The `client_secret` of the user's personal API key. Can also be set with the `VAULTWARDEN_CLIENT_SECRET` environment variable.

email.description: The email of the user to authenticate as. Can also be set with the `VAULTWARDEN_EMAIL` environment variable.

endpoint.description: The URL of the Vaultwarden server. Can also be set with the `VAULTWARDEN_ENDPOINT` environment variable.

master_password.description: The master password of the user, used to log in and to decrypt the user's keys. Can also be set with the `VAULTWARDEN_MASTER_PASSWORD` environment variable.

max_retry_wait.description: The total number of seconds a request waits for retries when Vaultwarden rate limits it (HTTP 429), for example when many provider instances log in from the same IP address. Retries back off exponentially. Set to `0` to disable retries. Defaults to `60`. Can also be set with the `VAULTWARDEN_MAX_RETRY_WAIT` environment variable.

block.description:
Terraform provider for [Vaultwarden](https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden), an unofficial Bitwarden-compatible server. It supports and is tested against the latest two Vaultwarden minor releases, currently 1.36.x and 1.37.x; older Vaultwarden versions get best-effort support only, and the provider warns when it detects one.

The provider authenticates in up to two ways, which can be combined:

- **As a user**, with `email` and `master_password`. Required for resources that act on behalf of a user, such as organizations and collections, because their data is encrypted client-side with the user's keys. If the user has two-step login enabled, also set the user's personal API key (`client_id` and `client_secret`).
- **As the server admin**, with `admin_token`. Required for resources that use the `/admin` API, such as `vaultwarden_user` and `vaultwarden_account_register`. The admin page must be enabled on the server.

Every attribute can also be set with an environment variable.

email.description: The email of the account to register. Changing it deletes the account, including its vault, and registers a new one.

name.description: The name of the account to register. Changing it deletes the account, including its vault, and registers a new one.

password.description: The password of the account to register. It is stored in plain text in the state: with Terraform 1.11 and later, use `password_wo` instead. Exactly one of `password` and `password_wo` must be set. Changing it deletes the account, including its vault, and registers a new one. The password cannot be read back, so it is not set after an import; setting it then only updates the state. Moving the same password to `password_wo` does not replace the account.

password_wo.description: The password of the account to register, as a write-only attribute that is never stored in the plan or state. Requires Terraform 1.11 or later. Exactly one of `password` and `password_wo` must be set. Terraform cannot detect changes of a write-only value: change `password_wo_version` to register the account again with a new password.

password_wo_version.description: Version of `password_wo`. Changing it deletes the account, including its vault, and registers a new one with the current `password_wo`. Setting it for the first time, for example after an import or when moving from `password` to `password_wo`, only updates the state.

block.description:
This resource registers a new account on the Vaultwarden server.

`password` is saved in plain text to the state. With Terraform 1.11 and later, use the write-only `password_wo` with `password_wo_version` instead, which are never stored.

Requires `admin_token` to be set in the provider configuration.

name.description: The name of the folder. Bitwarden clients show a name with slashes, such as `Parent/Child`, as a nested folder

block.description:
This resource creates a folder in the personal vault of the provider user. The folder name is encrypted with the user's key. Deleting a folder keeps the items in it and moves them out of the folder.

Requires `email` and `master_password` to be set in the provider configuration.

content.description: Content of the attachment, as a UTF-8 string. Requires `file_name`

content_base64.description: Content of the attachment, base64-encoded, for binary files. Requires `file_name`

content_sha256.description: Hex-encoded SHA-256 hash of the content of the attachment

file.description: Path of the file to attach. Exactly one of `file`, `content` and `content_base64` must be set

file_name.description: Name of the attachment. Defaults to the name of `file`. Changing it replaces the attachment

item_id.description: ID of the item to attach the file to. Changing it replaces the attachment

size.description: Size of the encrypted attachment in bytes

size_name.description: Size of the encrypted attachment in a human-readable form, such as `1.2 KB`

block.description:
This resource attaches a file to an item, in the personal vault of the provider user or in an organization. The file is encrypted like Bitwarden clients do: with its own attachment key, which is encrypted with the key of the item.

Attachments cannot be changed: a different content or file name replaces the attachment. Changes to the content are detected with its SHA-256 hash (`content_sha256`), so changing only the path of `file` keeps the attachment. Empty files are not supported. Use the `vaultwarden_item_attachment` ephemeral resource to read the content of an attachment.

Vaultwarden limits the storage of attachments with `USER_ATTACHMENT_LIMIT` and `ORG_ATTACHMENT_LIMIT`, and accepts files up to 525 MB.

Requires `email` and `master_password` to be set in the provider configuration.

collection_ids.description: IDs of the organization collections the item is assigned to. Requires `organization_id`. Defaults to none, which only organization owners and admins can use; other members must assign the item to a collection they can edit

favorite.description: Whether the item is a favorite of the provider user. Defaults to `false`

linked_id.description: For a `linked` field, the ID of the item attribute it links to, such as `100` for the username or `101` for the password of a login

name.description: The name of the custom field

type.description: The type of the custom field: `text`, `hidden`, `boolean` or `linked`. Defaults to `text`

value.description: The value of the custom field. For a `boolean` field, `true` or `false`. Linked fields have no value

fields.description: The custom fields of the item. Defaults to none

folder_id.description: ID of the provider user's folder that the item is in. Folders are personal: the item is shown in the folder only for the provider user, also for organization items

name.description: The name of the item

organization_id.description: ID of the organization that owns the item. Leave unset for an item in the personal vault of the provider user. Changing it replaces the item, because Bitwarden cannot move items out of an organization

password.description: The password of the login. When it changes, the previous password is added to the item's password history, like Bitwarden clients do

reprompt.description: Whether Bitwarden clients ask for the master password before showing the item. Defaults to `false`

totp.description: The TOTP secret or `otpauth://` URI of the login

match.description: How Bitwarden clients match the URI for autofill: `domain`, `host`, `starts_with`, `exact`, `regular_expression` or `never`. `null` uses the client's default

uris.description: The URIs of the login, for autofill. Defaults to none

block.description:
This resource creates a login item, with a username, password, TOTP secret and URIs, in the personal vault of the provider user or in an organization.

Items are encrypted client-side, like Bitwarden clients do: new items get their own item key (cipher key), which is encrypted with the key of the provider user or of the organization. Updates keep the parts of the item that the provider does not manage, such as the password history, passkeys and attachments. Deleting the item deletes it permanently, without moving it to the trash. An item moved to the trash outside Terraform is created again.

The secrets of the item, such as `notes`, are saved in the Terraform state. Requires `email` and `master_password` to be set in the provider configuration.

collection_ids.description: IDs of the organization collections the item is assigned to. Requires `organization_id`. Defaults to none, which only organization owners and admins can use; other members must assign the item to a collection they can edit

favorite.description: Whether the item is a favorite of the provider user. Defaults to `false`

linked_id.description: For a `linked` field, the ID of the item attribute it links to, such as `100` for the username or `101` for the password of a login

name.description: The name of the custom field

type.description: The type of the custom field: `text`, `hidden`, `boolean` or `linked`. Defaults to `text`

value.description: The value of the custom field. For a `boolean` field, `true` or `false`. Linked fields have no value

fields.description: The custom fields of the item. Defaults to none

folder_id.description: ID of the provider user's folder that the item is in. Folders are personal: the item is shown in the folder only for the provider user, also for organization items

name.description: The name of the item

organization_id.description: ID of the organization that owns the item. Leave unset for an item in the personal vault of the provider user. Changing it replaces the item, because Bitwarden cannot move items out of an organization

reprompt.description: Whether Bitwarden clients ask for the master password before showing the item. Defaults to `false`

block.description:
This resource creates a secure note item in the personal vault of the provider user or in an organization. The note's text is the `notes` attribute.

Items are encrypted client-side, like Bitwarden clients do: new items get their own item key (cipher key), which is encrypted with the key of the provider user or of the organization. Updates keep the parts of the item that the provider does not manage, such as the password history, passkeys and attachments. Deleting the item deletes it permanently, without moving it to the trash. An item moved to the trash outside Terraform is created again.

The secrets of the item, such as `notes`, are saved in the Terraform state. Requires `email` and `master_password` to be set in the provider configuration.

billing_email.description: The billing email of the organization. If not specified, defaults to the authenticated user's email.

collection_name.description: The name of the collection to create for the organization. Defaults to `Default`

name.description: The name of the organization

block.description: This resource creates a Vaultwarden organization.

organization_id.description: ID of the organization. Changing it rotates the key of the new organization.

revision_date.description: When the API key was last rotated.

triggers.description: Arbitrary values that rotate the key again when they change, for example the `id` of a `time_rotating` resource.

block.description:
Rotates the API key of an organization: creating the resource, or replacing it when `triggers` change, gives the organization a new client secret and invalidates the old one. The secret is not stored: read it with the `vaultwarden_organization_api_key` ephemeral resource.

Destroying the resource leaves the current key unchanged. Rotating requires the provider user's master password and, on Vaultwarden 1.37 and later, the `Owner` role in the organization (1.36 also allows `Admin`).

external_id.description: An optional identifier that can be assigned to the collection for integration with external systems. This identifier is not generated by Vaultwarden and must be provided explicitly. It is typically used to link the collection to external systems, such as directory services (e.g., LDAP, Active Directory) or custom automation workflows.

name.description: The name of the organization collection

organization_id.description: ID of the organization that the collection belongs to

block.description: This resource creates a Vaultwarden organization collection.

group_id.description: ID of the group, for example `vaultwarden_organization_group.example.id`

hide_passwords.description: Whether passwords are hidden from the members of the group. Defaults to `false`

id.description: ID of the collection access, in the format `<organization_id>/<collection_id>/<group_id>`

manage.description: Whether the members of the group can manage the collection, including its access. Vaultwarden reports a group that can edit the items and see their passwords as able to manage the collection, so `manage = false` is not reported as drift in that case. Defaults to `false`

read_only.description: Whether the members of the group can only view the items in the collection. Defaults to `false`

block.description:
This resource gives a group access to a collection.

Access of other users and groups to the collection is left unchanged. Groups require the `ORG_GROUPS_ENABLED=true` setting on the Vaultwarden server.

hide_passwords.description: Whether passwords are hidden from the user. Defaults to `false`

id.description: ID of the collection access, in the format `<organization_id>/<collection_id>/<organization_user_id>`

manage.description: Whether the user can manage the collection, including its access. A `Manager` that can edit the collection and see its passwords can always manage it. Defaults to `false`

organization_user_id.description: ID of the organization user, for example `vaultwarden_organization_user.example.id`

read_only.description: Whether the user can only view the items in the collection. Defaults to `false`

block.description:
This resource gives an organization user access to a collection.

Access of other users and groups to the collection is left unchanged. Users with access to all collections (`Owner`, `Admin`, or a `Manager` with `access_all`) cannot be assigned to individual collections.

access_all.description: Whether the members of the group have access to all collections of the organization. Defaults to `false`. Vaultwarden 1.37 and later do not return this value, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected on those versions

external_id.description: An identifier to link the group to an external system, such as a directory service. Vaultwarden cannot change the external ID of an existing group, so changing it replaces the group

name.description: The name of the group

organization_id.description: ID of the organization that the group belongs to

block.description:
This resource creates a group in a Vaultwarden organization.

Groups require the `ORG_GROUPS_ENABLED=true` setting on the Vaultwarden server. Updates keep the group's members and collection access, including ones managed outside Terraform.

group_id.description: ID of the group, for example `vaultwarden_organization_group.example.id`

id.description: ID of the group membership, in the format `<organization_id>/<group_id>/<organization_user_id>`

organization_user_id.description: ID of the organization user, for example `vaultwarden_organization_user.example.id`

block.description:
This resource adds an organization user to a group.

Other members of the group and other groups of the user are left unchanged. Groups require the `ORG_GROUPS_ENABLED=true` setting on the Vaultwarden server.

data.description: The settings of the policy as a JSON object, for the policy types that have settings, for example `jsonencode({ minLength = 12, requireUpper = true })` for `master_password`. The keys are the ones the Bitwarden clients use, such as `minComplexity`, `minLength`, `requireUpper`, `requireLower`, `requireNumbers` and `requireSpecial` for `master_password`, `disableHideEmail` for `send_options`, and `autoEnrollEnabled` for `reset_password`.

id.description: ID of the policy, in the format `<organization_id>/<type>`

type.description: The type of the policy. One of `disable_send`, `master_password`, `organization_user_notification`, `password_generator`, `personal_ownership`, `remove_unlock_with_pin`, `reset_password`, `restricted_item_types`, `send_options`, `single_org`, `two_factor_authentication`, `uri_match_defaults`. `personal_ownership` is the *Remove individual vault* policy, and `reset_password` the *Account recovery administration* policy. `organization_user_notification` requires Vaultwarden 1.37 or later.

block.description:
This resource manages a policy of an organization.

Policies cannot be deleted: destroying the resource disables the policy and clears its data. Enabling some policies changes the organization's members: `two_factor_authentication` revokes members without two-step login, and `single_org` revokes members that belong to another organization. Owners and Admins are exempt.

access_all.description: Whether the user has access to all collections in the organization. `Owner` and `Admin` users always have access to all collections. For `Manager` users it can be set to `true` (the *Manage all collections* permission). `User` users cannot have it; grant them access to individual collections instead. Defaults to `true` for `Owner` and `Admin`, and `false` otherwise.

auto_confirm.description: Whether to confirm the user once they have accepted the invitation. Until a user is confirmed, they cannot decrypt the organization's items. Confirming encrypts the organization key with the user's public key, which Vaultwarden only allows after the user accepted the invitation. When the user has accepted, the plan shows `status` as changing and the apply confirms them; while they are still `Invited`, nothing changes. Setting it to `false` does not unconfirm a confirmed user. Defaults to `false`.

email.description: The email of the user to invite. Changing it removes the user from the organization and invites the new email.

organization_id.description: ID of the organization to invite the user to

revoked.description: Whether the user's access to the organization is revoked. A revoked user stays in the organization but cannot access its items; restoring them (`false`) brings back the status they had before. Defaults to `false`.

status.description: The status of the user: `Invited`, `Accepted`, `Confirmed` or `Revoked`

type.description: The role type of the user (Owner, Admin, User, Manager). Defaults to `User`

block.description: This resource invites a user to an organization on the Vaultwarden server.

email.description: The email of the user to invite. Changing it deletes the user, including their vault if they accepted the invitation, and invites the new email.

enabled.description: Whether the user can log in. Disabling a user also logs them out of all their devices. Defaults to `true`.

This resource invites a user to the Vaultwarden server.

Requires `admin_token` to be set in the provider configuration.

Requires `admin_token` to be set in the provider configuration.

created_at.description: When the user was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC

email_verified.description: Whether the user has verified their email. Always `true` when the server has no SMTP configured

enabled.description: Whether the user is enabled. A disabled user cannot log in

invited.description: Whether the user was invited and has not created an account (set a master password) yet

last_active.description: When the user was last active, as Vaultwarden formats it for display: `YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss` and a time zone abbreviation, in the server's time zone (the `TZ` environment variable). `null` when the user has never logged in

name.description: The name of the user, `null` when empty. Vaultwarden sets the name of an invited user to their email
The name of the organization

organization_user_id.description: The ID of the user's membership in the organization

type.description: The type of the user in the organization: `Owner`, `Admin`, `User` or `Manager`

organizations.description: The organizations the user is a confirmed member of, sorted by name. Organizations the user is only invited to, or has accepted but is not yet confirmed in, are not listed

two_factor_enabled.description: Whether the user has two-step login enabled

users.description: The users of the server, sorted by email

block.description:
Use this data source to list all users of the Vaultwarden server, including invited users.

Requires `admin_token` to be set in the provider configuration.
